name: Hebes Mensa deposit
credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona. DTM produced at HiROC by Raymundo "R@y" Olguin.
geo_note: Hebes Chasma is an enclosed trough in the Valles Marineris system with no outlet. Hebes Mensa, the massive interior layered deposit, rises ~8 km from the chasma floor. Sulfate and phyllosilicate-bearing ILDs record prolonged aqueous diagenesis and are among the thickest sedimentary sequences on Mars.

name: Landon Valles basin
credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona. DTM produced at HiROC by Raymundo "R@y" Olguin.
geo_note: Landon Valles is a Noachian valley network system recording peak fluvial activity ~3.7 Ga. Basin-filling lacustrine sediments in the terminal basin potentially preserve a habitability record from early Mars. The global valley network mapping by Hynek et al. classifies this as a second-order tributary system.

name: Noachis Terra Craters
credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona. DTM produced at HiROC by Raymundo "R@y" Olguin.
geo_note: Noachis Terra is among the oldest preserved terrains on Mars (~4.0 Ga), densely cratered and dissected by Noachian valley networks. Impact craters preserve phyllosilicate-bearing ejecta blankets, and the valley network density records peak fluvial activity during the late Noachian–early Hesperian transition.

name: Arcadia Planitia
credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona. DTM produced at HiROC by Raymundo "R@y" Olguin.
geo_note: Arcadia Planitia in the northern lowlands hosts some of the highest near-surface ice content inferred on Mars from neutron spectrometry. Scalloped depressions, polygon networks, and layered ejecta craters record active periglacial processes driven by Amazonian ground ice.

name: Chaos Terrain
credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona. DTM produced at HiROC by Raymundo "R@y" Olguin.
geo_note: Martian chaotic terrain forms through catastrophic subsidence following drainage of subsurface volatiles, ice or pressurized groundwater. The resulting knobby remnant mesas and intervening depressions are genetically linked to outflow channel initiation and some of the largest known flood events in the Solar System.

name: Gullies Tempe Terra
credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona. DTM produced at HiROC by Raymundo "R@y" Olguin.
geo_note: Tempe Terra hosts one of the densest concentrations of Martian gullies, alcove-channel-apron systems incised into crater walls and hillslopes. Their geologically recent formation age and morphology suggest seasonal CO₂ frost-driven debris flows as the dominant formation mechanism.

name: Gorgonum Chaos
credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona. DTM produced at HiROC by Raymundo "R@y" Olguin.
geo_note: Gorgonum Chaos in Terra Sirenum is a chaotic depression associated with concentrated chloride and sulfate salt deposits, among the largest chloride exposures on Mars. One of the densest gully fields on Mars is also found here, interpreted as evidence of recent episodic liquid water activity.

name: Uranius Mons Crater
credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona. DTM produced at HiROC by Raymundo "R@y" Olguin.
geo_note: Uranius Mons is a low-relief paterae-type shield volcano in the Tharsis region. Impact craters on its flanks record multiple Amazonian resurfacing episodes. Its summit caldera and radial graben system indicate a complex magmatic history distinct from the large Tharsis Montes.

name: Aeolis Planum
credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona. DTM produced at HiROC by Raymundo "R@y" Olguin.
geo_note: Aeolis Planum flanks Gale Crater and hosts an extensive yardang field, wind-sculpted ridges formed by differential erosion of indurated sedimentary layers. The region records late Hesperian to Amazonian aeolian reworking of lacustrine deposits adjacent to the MSL Curiosity rover field site.

name: Phlegra Montes Valley
credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona. DTM produced at HiROC by Raymundo "R@y" Olguin.
geo_note: Phlegra Montes is a NW-trending mountain range bordering the northern lowlands, with valley systems exhibiting lobate debris aprons, the surface expression of debris-covered glaciers. These represent the most direct evidence for extant non-polar ground ice on Mars.

name: Pasteur Crater
credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona. DTM produced at HiROC by Raymundo "R@y" Olguin.
geo_note: Pasteur Crater in Arabia Terra contains finely-laminated interior layered deposits (ILDs) interpreted as aeolian or lacustrine sedimentary sequences. Arabia Terra hosts one of Mars' largest concentrations of layered sedimentary basins, potentially recording Hesperian hydrological activity.

name: Olympus Mons Systems
credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona. DTM produced at HiROC by Raymundo "R@y" Olguin.
geo_note: Olympus Mons is the largest shield volcano in the Solar System, rising ~22 km above the surrounding plains with a basal escarpment exceeding 8 km. Lava flow systems on the flanks preserve primary Amazonian volcanic stratigraphy; the summit caldera records multiple collapse episodes from complex magmatic evolution.

name: Argyre Planitia Valley
credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona. DTM produced at HiROC by Raymundo "R@y" Olguin.
geo_note: Argyre Planitia is a 1,800 km impact basin reaching −5.2 km, the deepest on Mars. Valley networks on its rim record late Noachian fluvial incision, and glacial flow indicators including lobate debris aprons suggest Late Amazonian ice sheet occupation of the basin interior.

name: Oxia Colles
credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona. DTM produced at HiROC by Raymundo "R@y" Olguin.
geo_note: Oxia Colles forms the knobby highland remnant terrain on the western margin of the clay-bearing Oxia Planum plain. These erosional remnants of Noachian crust at the crustal dichotomy boundary expose Fe/Mg smectite-bearing bedrock detected by CRISM and OMEGA spectrometers.

name: Coogoon Valles
credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona. DTM produced at HiROC by Raymundo "R@y" Olguin.
geo_note: Coogoon Valles is a sinuous valley system draining into Oxia Planum, the ExoMars Rosalind Franklin landing site. Its delta fan at the basin outlet preserves Noachian fluvial and lacustrine sediments rich in Fe/Mg phyllosilicates, making it a key astrobiological target.

name: Aram Chaos
credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona. DTM produced at HiROC by Raymundo "R@y" Olguin.
geo_note: Aram Chaos is a ~280 km crater that collapsed catastrophically following destabilization of a subsurface cryosphere. TES grey hematite detections indicate past aqueous mineralization. The chaotic knobby interior records some of Mars' most violent water-release events.

name: South Polar Deposits
credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona. DTM produced at HiROC by Raymundo "R@y" Olguin.
geo_note: Near 89°S the SPLD residual cap hosts active CO₂ slab sublimation features ('swiss-cheese terrain') documenting present-day volatile transport. HiRISE multi-temporal imaging revealed annual changes in these features, providing a direct record of modern Martian climate.

name: North Polar Layered Deposits Bench
credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona. DTM produced at HiROC by Raymundo "R@y" Olguin.
geo_note: North Polar Layered Deposit bench scarps expose ~2 km of stratigraphy spanning ~5 Myr of obliquity-paced accumulation. SHARAD detected internal unconformities interpreted as high-obliquity erosional episodes. Individual layers 1–10 m thick serve as a Martian equivalent of ice-core climate proxies.

name: South Polar Deposits
credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona. DTM produced at HiROC by Raymundo "R@y" Olguin.
geo_note: The South Polar Layered Deposits (SPLD) are a ~3 km-thick stack of alternating ice-rich and dust-laden layers recording obliquity-driven Martian climate cycles over tens of millions of years. SHARAD radar soundings resolved the internal stratigraphy and confirmed near-pure water ice composition.

name: Cavil Angusti South Polar
credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona. DTM produced at HiROC by Raymundo "R@y" Olguin.
geo_note: Cavi Angusti comprises deep, steep-walled pits cut into the Hesperian Dorsa Argentea Formation beside the south polar layered deposits. The formation is interpreted as the deposit of a former south circumpolar ice sheet that melted and retreated; here the cavi expose ~1.7 km of relief.

name: Brain Terrain
credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona. DTM produced at HiROC by Raymundo "R@y" Olguin.
geo_note: Brain terrain is a convoluted ridge-and-cell surface texture, ~3–5 m in relief, formed by the sublimation of buried mid-latitude excess ice. Its closed-cell morphology is a diagnostic marker of subsurface volatile loss and ground-ice degradation in the northern mid-latitudes.

name: Terra Sirenum
credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona. DTM produced at HiROC by Raymundo "R@y" Olguin.
geo_note: Terra Sirenum is a heavily cratered Noachian highland hosting chloride salt deposits and Fe/Mg phyllosilicates. These mineral assemblages record ancient aqueous environments and episodic surface water, making the region a key archive of early Martian habitability in the southern hemisphere.

name: SpaceX Starship Arcadia
credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona. DTM produced at HiROC by Raymundo "R@y" Olguin.
geo_note: Arcadia Planitia is a smooth northern mid-latitude plain underlain in places by a widespread, decameters-thick layer of excess water ice. Terraced impact craters and SHARAD radar reflections indicate that this buried ice is volumetrically significant, making the region important for periglacial stratigraphy, recent climate history, and future landing-site resource assessment.

name: Protonilus Mensae Ridges
credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona. DTM produced at HiROC by Raymundo "R@y" Olguin.
geo_note: Protonilus Mensae lies along the northern dichotomy boundary in classic fretted terrain containing lobate debris aprons and lineated valley fill. These flow-related landforms are widely interpreted as remnants of Late Amazonian debris-covered glacial systems, preserving evidence for substantial mid-latitude ice accumulation and subsequent sublimation beneath protective debris.

name: Phlegra Dorsa Cone Field
credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona. DTM produced at HiROC by Raymundo "R@y" Olguin.
geo_note: Phlegra Dorsa contains abundant small-cone morphologies whose spatial patterns contribute to studies of Martian volcanic, sedimentary, and periglacial processes. High-resolution HiRISE mapping of cone fields provides morphometric constraints on cone geometry and distribution, supporting comparison among competing formation mechanisms across Mars.

name: High Latitude Exposure
credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona. DTM produced at HiROC by Raymundo "R@y" Olguin.
geo_note: The north polar layered deposits are a thick sequence of water-ice-rich and dust-bearing strata exposed in troughs near Planum Boreum. HiRISE stereo DTMs resolve the topographic expression of individual layers and permit stratigraphic correlations through hundreds of meters of section, supporting interpretation of the NPLD as a high-resolution archive of recent Martian climate variability.

name: Pits Sinai Planum
credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona. DTM produced at HiROC by Raymundo "R@y" Olguin.
geo_note: Sinai Planum is part of the tectonically fractured plateau surrounding the Valles Marineris–Tharsis region, where pits and troughs commonly occur with extensional structures. Martian pit-crater chains are generally interpreted as collapse features developed above subsurface cavities, and structural associations indicate that dilational normal faults and extension fractures are a major formation mechanism.

name: Mesa Utopia Planitia
credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona. DTM produced at HiROC by Raymundo "R@y" Olguin.
geo_note: Utopia Planitia occupies a giant Noachian impact basin in the northern lowlands whose present morphology reflects extensive sedimentary and volcanic infilling as well as later tectonic modification. Mesas and other remnant relief within the plains preserve local stratigraphic and structural information that helps constrain the basin's long post-impact resurfacing history.

name: Bernard Crater Channels
credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona. DTM produced at HiROC by Raymundo "R@y" Olguin.
geo_note: Bernard Crater is a large impact basin in the Terra Sirenum highlands. Sinuous channels incised into its floor record surface or near-surface water flow after the crater formed, linking this site to the broader record of valley-network activity that shaped the southern highlands during the Noachian and early Hesperian.

name: Maja Valles
credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona. DTM produced at HiROC by Raymundo "R@y" Olguin.
geo_note: Maja Valles is a large outflow channel that drains from the Valles Marineris region northward across Lunae Planum into Chryse Planitia. Streamlined islands, scoured floors, and cataracts record catastrophic Hesperian floods released from the subsurface. The README notes extra noise on the west side of this DTM from jitter in the parent stereo pair; consult the FOM map before analysis.

name: Crater Adjacent Lunae Mensa
credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona. DTM produced at HiROC by Raymundo "R@y" Olguin.
geo_note: This crater sits against the Lunae Mensa scarp at the eastern edge of the Kasei Valles flood system, where catastrophic outflow carved kilometer-scale cliffs into Lunae Planum. With nearly 2.75 km of relief, the DTM captures the scarp, the crater, and the scoured channel floor in a single product.

name: Small Mounds Chryse Planitia
credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona. DTM produced at HiROC by Raymundo "R@y" Olguin.
geo_note: Chryse Planitia hosts fields of small, often cratered mounds at the terminus of the circum-Chryse outflow channels. Their morphology and setting have been compared with terrestrial mud volcanoes, which would point to fluid-rich sediment rising from depth after the floods. This DTM has the lowest total RMS (0.090 px) in the portfolio.

name: Flute Casts Ares Vallis
credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona. DTM produced at HiROC by Raymundo "R@y" Olguin.
geo_note: Ares Vallis is one of the major outflow channels draining into Chryse Planitia near the Mars Pathfinder landing site. Possible flute casts, scour marks formed by turbulent flood water eroding the channel floor, preserve the flow direction and energy of the catastrophic floods that carved the valley.

name: Terraced Crater
credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona. DTM produced at HiROC by Raymundo "R@y" Olguin.
geo_note: This terraced crater formed on the ejecta of a larger crater in the northern mid-latitudes. Terraces inside small craters form when an impact excavates a layered target with a strength contrast, such as an ice-rich layer over stronger material, so terrace depths can be used to estimate the thickness of buried excess ice.

name: Troughs Ridges Chryse Planitia
credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona. DTM produced at HiROC by Raymundo "R@y" Olguin.
geo_note: At the northern reach of Chryse Planitia, where the circum-Chryse outflow channels open into the northern lowlands, troughs and ridges cut the plains. Trough networks in the northern plains have long been used to test how the thick lowland fill compacted, cooled, and deformed after emplacement, so measured trough widths, depths, and wall slopes from this DTM constrain those models directly.

name: Dunes Kaltain
credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona. DTM produced at HiROC by Raymundo "R@y" Olguin.
geo_note: The Kaltain dunes lie in the north polar sand sea that rings the residual ice cap. Each winter a seasonal carbon-dioxide frost layer blankets the dunes; as it sublimates in spring, gas flow and frost-driven slumping erode the slip faces, and summer winds restore them, making this field a monitor of present-day sediment transport. The README cautions that the dunes leave significant artifacts at short wavelengths; consult the FOM map before measuring small-scale topography.

name: Dark Linear Ridges Southern
credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona. DTM produced at HiROC by Raymundo "R@y" Olguin.
geo_note: Dark linear ridges cross the southern high-latitude highlands here. Elongate ridges in the circum-south-polar region are commonly interpreted as eskers deposited beneath a former Hesperian ice sheet or as resistant, inverted channel fills; with about 164 m of relief at 2 m post spacing, this DTM provides the cross-sectional profiles needed to tell those origins apart.

name: Landing SpaceX Starship Phlegra
credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona. DTM produced at HiROC by Raymundo "R@y" Olguin.
geo_note: This DTM covers terrain in the Phlegra region of the northern mid-latitudes that has been studied as a candidate landing area for SpaceX Starship. Radar, thermal, and geomorphic mapping by the Subsurface Water Ice Mapping (SWIM) project shows that water ice is likely within the upper few meters across much of this belt: a resource for future crewed missions and a constraint on landing-site engineering. Its mean offset from MOLA (-0.017 m) is the smallest in the portfolio.

name: Guilled Crater
credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona. DTM produced at HiROC by Raymundo "R@y" Olguin.
geo_note: This southern mid-latitude crater contains well-developed gullies on steep interior slopes. Martian gullies commonly consist of alcoves, channels, and depositional aprons, and repeat HiRISE imaging has shown that present-day modification at many mid- and high-latitude sites is strongly associated with seasonal carbon-dioxide frost processes.

name: USGS Dune
credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona. DTM produced at HiROC by Raymundo "R@y" Olguin.
geo_note: This high-southern-latitude dune field provides topographic control on dune morphology in a terrain affected by strong seasonal carbon-dioxide frost cycles. Repeat HiRISE observations of polar and subpolar dunes show that frost-related mass movement can modify dune slopes and gullies on present-day Mars.
